note: Hand-written by the harness author, who knows the answers: for developing the pipeline, never reported as the result. Each need is a complex, module-scale capability, written without the target's identifier. targets: acceptable roots as pkg:file#name ('*' = any file in the package, for packages that ship several builds); [] means nothing in the corpus implements it. The held-out set comes from needs-from-readme.mjs.

queries.need: Parse CSV text into an array of records, handling quoted fields that contain the delimiter or newlines, doubled quotes inside quotes, a configurable delimiter, and optionally using the first line as column names.
Given a list of semantic version strings and a range expression such as '^1.2.0 || >=2.5 <3', return the highest version that satisfies the range, or null when none does.
Check whether a semantic version satisfies a range expression, including caret, tilde and hyphen ranges, x-ranges and '||' alternatives, with an option for loose parsing.
Find the lowest semantic version that could possibly match a range expression.
Decide whether every version matched by one semantic-version range is also matched by another range.
Parse an ISO 8601 date-time string, including calendar, week and ordinal dates, an optional time with fractions and an optional timezone offset, into a Date; give an invalid date for malformed input.
Format a date as an ISO 8601 string with the date, the time and the local timezone offset, with options for the basic or extended format and date-only or time-only output.
Make a deep copy of any value, including nested objects and arrays, Maps, Sets, Dates, regular expressions, typed arrays and buffers, preserving circular references and prototypes.
Recursively merge the properties of source objects into a destination object, merging nested plain objects and arrays rather than replacing them.
Wrap a function so it runs at most once per wait interval, with options to call it on the leading edge, the trailing edge, or both.
Wrap a function so calls are postponed until a given time has passed since the last call, with leading and trailing options, a maximum wait, and the ability to cancel or flush a pending call.
Set a value at a deep property path such as 'a[0].b.c' in an object, creating the missing objects and arrays along the way.
A key-value cache bounded by entry count or total size that evicts the least recently used entries, with optional time-to-live per entry, stale reads, and a fetch method that fills missing entries.
Limit how many promise-returning tasks run at the same time: queue the rest and start them as running ones finish, and report the active and pending counts.
Throttle an async function so it is called at most a given number of times per time interval, queuing the excess calls, with optional strict mode and abort.
Validate an email address with options for allowing a display name, requiring a top-level domain, allowing IP addresses as the domain, and limiting the length of each part.
Validate a URL string with options for the allowed protocols, requiring a protocol or a top-level domain, allowing underscores or IP hosts, and checking the port and the host whitelist.
Canonicalize an email address for comparison: lowercase it and apply provider-specific rules, such as removing dots and plus-suffixes for Gmail addresses.
Check whether a password is strong enough by minimum length and minimum counts of lowercase letters, uppercase letters, digits and symbols, or return a numeric strength score.
Generate a time-ordered unique identifier from a millisecond timestamp and random bits, monotonic within the same millisecond, in the standard 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form.
Generate a deterministic unique identifier from a namespace identifier and a name by hashing them with SHA-1, in the standard 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form.
Compute the MD5 digest of a sequence of bytes.
Compute the SHA-1 digest of a sequence of bytes.
Find the string in a list that needs the fewest single-character edits to become a given word, fast even for long strings.

Define a schema for an object with typed fields, then validate unknown input against it, returning the typed value or a list of issues, each with the path of the invalid field; support strict, passthrough and partial variants.
A schema for strings that can require a minimum or maximum length, a regular expression, or a format such as email, URL, UUID or ISO date-time, and trims or lowercases as part of parsing.
Decode base64 text into bytes, handling padding and rejecting input whose length is not a multiple of four.
Sort the nodes of a dependency graph given as edges so that each node comes after its dependencies, failing when there is a cycle.
Compile a JSON Pointer once into an object with get and set operations that apply it to many documents.
Make a generator of random identifiers of a given length drawn from a custom alphabet, using a secure random source.
Parse a YAML document into plain objects, arrays and scalars, including anchors and multi-line strings.
Render Markdown text to HTML, including headings, lists, links, emphasis and fenced code blocks.
Compress a byte array with the DEFLATE algorithm and decompress it again.
Parse a cron expression and compute the next times it fires after a given date.
Compute a line-by-line difference between two texts as a list of added, removed and unchanged lines.
Match URL paths against route patterns such as '/users/:id/posts/:postId' and extract the named parameters.
Format a number as a currency amount with locale-aware digit grouping, decimal separator and currency symbol placement.
Resize an RGBA image buffer to new dimensions with bilinear interpolation.
